daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo is considering creating a new agency to regulate government procurement of goods and services, after stating that procurement leakages could cost Indonesia US$21 billion. The president also emphasized that Indonesia's market reforms are driven by national interests rather than foreign pressure. Separately, Prabowo urged financial institutions to prioritize national interests in their operations.

  • The Constitutional Court is examining how DPR and government will respond after the Police Law was declared procedurally flawed.
  • A DPR member stated the revision of the State Defence Law must anticipate threats over the next 20 years.
  • Police investigators examined former National Narcotics Agency chief Komjen Marthinus Hukom as a witness in the treason case, with Hukom testifying that former police chief Listyo Sigit used Densus 88 personnel for political operations.
  • Bareskrim interrogated Budi Arie and former Gibran aide in connection with the treason case.
  • National Police dismissed Kombes Iman Imanuddin for ordering a case termination.
  • The Constitutional Court questioned the rationale for changing the maximum number of presidential advisors from nine to unlimited based on presidential needs.
  • The PKB party organized a political literacy program for 150 student council members from Greater Jakarta.
  • The government changed civil service regulations to allow new civil servants to request transfers after five years of service.
  • Presidential Communications Office dismissed Ulta Levenia effective 1 November 2026.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia secured entry into the CPTPP accession process, according to a minister. President Prabowo highlighted Indonesia's strategic importance by comparing Indonesia's waters with the Strait of Hormuz. This diplomatic milestone comes as Indonesia strengthens its trade relationships in the Asia-Pacific region.

  • Indonesia is targeting bilateral trade with the UAE to surpass US$8 billion by 2030.
  • The Foreign Ministry said Indonesia and Poland have potential to become a bridge between Southeast Asia and Europe.
  • Indonesia strengthened tourism diplomacy through the UN Tourism General Assembly.
  • Indonesia trained 49 maritime professionals from 13 African countries.
  • Australia is strengthening gender equality partnerships with Indonesia and ASEAN.

Other

Bank Indonesia projects economic growth of 6 percent in 2027, while forecasting bank credit growth to accelerate to 9-13 percent. The central bank outlined five policy pillars to optimize resource downstreaming and will reinforce monetary policy to guard the rupiah and control inflation, though global uncertainty could challenge the growth target.

  • Indonesia is reviewing energy subsidies following an OECD recommendation.
  • The government is preparing three measures to address US AI chip export controls.
  • Environmental authorities are investigating hundreds of corporations over forest and land fires.
  • Prosecutors allege Riza Chalid and Irawan Prakoso were enriched by 543 million US dollars in a crude oil management corruption case.
  • The national online shopping festival targets transactions of Rp 37-39 trillion involving 2,000 businesses.
